pi_api_missing:
Works, but missing APIs (Numverify/APILayer)
in .env for advanced information.
metadata_deps_missing: Pillow and PyPDF2 missing. Run pip install pillow pypdf2.
metadata_partial: Partial dependencies. Some file types won't be analysable.
whois_ok: WHOIS/DNS module ready. No configuration required.
wayback_ok: Wayback Machine module ready (Archive.org CDX API).
pi_no_exec:
Binary found but it is not executable.
Run: chmod +x phoneinfoga
chk_insecure_ssl_tip:
Disables validation of the server certificate.
Use it only to audit pre-production hosts with broken TLS:
an expired or spoofed certificate will no longer be detected.
chk_google_search_tip:
Runs Google Dorks over variants of the number.
It issues many queries: Google may show you a captcha.
help_holehe_body: Checks about 120 services (Spotify, Twitter, Adobe...) to see whether an account exists for that email. It also looks up whether the address shows up in public data breaches.
help_holehe_gives: services where it is registered and breaches it appears in
help_sherlock_body: Looks for the same handle across hundreds of social networks and forums. Useful to see whether someone reuses the same name everywhere, which is the norm.
help_sherlock_needs: the handle only, no @ and no web address
help_sherlock_gives: direct links to the profiles found
help_phoneinfoga_desc: Where a number is from and who operates it
help_phoneinfoga_body: Identifies country, carrier and line type (landline or mobile). If you tick the box, it also builds Google searches with the number written in several different formats.
help_phoneinfoga_gives: country, carrier, line type and search links
help_virustotal_desc: Whether a site is flagged as dangerous
help_virustotal_body: Asks about 90 antivirus engines what they think of that domain or IP. Use it before opening a link you do not trust. 0 out of 90 does not prove it is safe, but several flags is a bad sign.
help_virustotal_needs: a domain or an IP. Requires a free API key in .env
help_virustotal_gives: how many engines flag it as malicious, suspicious or clean
help_whois_desc: Who registered the domain and where it points
help_whois_body:
The registration record: who signed it up, when, and until when. Plus the servers it points to right now.

Usually the best starting point for a domain: the IP it finds feeds the other tools.
help_whois_needs: the bare domain: example.com (no https:// or www)
help_whois_gives: registrar, registration and expiry dates, DNS servers and IP
help_subdomains_desc: Other names hidden under the same domain
help_subdomains_body:
Finds addresses like mail.example.com or api.example.com. That is where internal panels, staging environments and services nobody meant to publish tend to show up.

When it finishes it opens an interactive graph in your browser.
help_subdomains_gives: a list of subdomains and a graph relating them
help_ports_desc: Which services it exposes to the internet
help_ports_body:
An open port is a door where that server accepts connections: 22 is remote access (SSH), 443 is secure web, 3306 is a database that probably should not be visible from outside.

It is passive: it queries Shodan's database and sends not a single packet to the target.
help_ports_gives: the list of open ports as seen from outside
help_headers_desc: Whether a site has its protections switched on
help_headers_body:
A website can send the browser a set of security instructions. When they are missing, the site is easier to attack:

  HSTS     forces an encrypted connection
  CSP      limits which code is allowed to run
  X-Frame  stops it being embedded to trick you
help_headers_needs: a domain or a full address
help_headers_gives: which protections are in place and which are missing
help_wayback_desc: What that site looked like years ago
help_wayback_body:
The internet archive has kept copies of websites since 1996. This finds the oldest copy that exists of this one.

Useful to learn how long a site has existed, or to see content its owner has already deleted.
help_wayback_needs: a domain or a full address
help_wayback_gives: the date of the oldest copy and the link to view it
help_metadata_desc: The hidden data inside a photo or a PDF
help_metadata_body:
Cameras and software leave information tucked inside files: what took it, when, with which program and, in many photos, the exact GPS coordinates of the place.

It reads files on your own machine, it downloads nothing.
help_metadata_needs: the path to an image or PDF (use the folder button)
help_metadata_gives: camera, dates, software used and GPS coordinates if present
